source.text: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה־הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ הַבִּ֖יטָה וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת־חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember, Yahweh, what has happened to us; look and see our disgrace.

en.L: Remember, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what has happened to us; \q look and see our disgrace.
en.B: Remember, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what has come upon us; \q look, and see how we are put to shame.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember what has happened to us. \q Look and see how we are scorned.

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, de ce qui nous est arrivé ; \q regarde et vois notre opprobre.
fr.B: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, de ce qui nous est survenu ; \q regarde, et vois comme on nous couvre de honte.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de ce qui nous est arrivé. \q Regarde et vois comme on nous méprise.

es.L: Acuérdate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, de lo que nos ha sucedido; \q mira y ve nuestra afrenta.
es.B: Acuérdate, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, de lo que nos ha pasado; \q mira y fíjate en cómo nos cubren de vergüenza.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, acuérdate de lo que nos ha pasado. \q Mira y ve cómo nos desprecian.

sw.L: Kumbuka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yaliyotupata; \q tazama uone aibu yetu.
sw.B: Kumbuka, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, yale yaliyotujia; \q tazama, uone jinsi tulivyoaibishwa.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kumbuka yaliyotupata. \q Tazama uone jinsi tunavyodharauliwa.

vi.L: Xin nhớ, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, điều đã xảy đến cho chúng con; \q xin nhìn và xem sự sỉ nhục của chúng con.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ lại những gì đã giáng trên chúng con; \q xin đoái xem chúng con bị sỉ nhục thế nào.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin nhớ những gì đã xảy ra cho chúng con. \q Xin nhìn xem chúng con bị khinh bỉ thế nào.

decisions.choice: twenty-two verses, not an alphabet poem: a prayer of the whole people
decisions.reason: Chapters 1-4 are alphabetic poems, each verse (in chapter 3 each group of three verses) starting with the next letter from aleph to taw. This last chapter keeps the number twenty-two, the number of letters, but its verses do not follow the alphabet. Its lines are also more evenly balanced than the long-and-short lament rhythm of chapters 1-4. The voice changes too: the whole community now speaks as "we" and prays directly to God, as in the communal laments of the Psalms (Psalms 44, 74, 79). The prayer runs to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: remember: take note and act
decisions.reason: When people ask God to remember, they are not asking him to recall a fact he has forgotten but to pay attention and do something about it (Genesis 8:1; Psalm 74:2, 18). The same plea about the scorn God's people bear is made in Psalm 89:51.

decisions.choice: our disgrace: the scorn others heap on us
decisions.reason: The word (cherpah) is the taunting and contempt of onlookers (Psalm 79:4; Jeremiah 24:9). The people ask God to see how low they have been brought in the eyes of the nations.

decisions.choice: LORD, remember ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the name first, as people commonly begin a prayer in plain English.

decisions.choice: the whole people prays: "nos", with "tú" to God
decisions.reason: The last poem is the people's prayer in the first person plural, spoken to the LORD with "tú", as every Spanish prayer in these books is; the vocative "SEÑOR" again takes no "oh".

decisions.choice: The whole people pray as "chúng con", with "Lạy CHÚA, xin ..." and "Ngài" for God, through the chapter
decisions.reason: Chapter 5 is a prayer of the whole people; "chúng con" is the word a community uses for itself before God, as in 3:42–47, and "xin" makes each imperative a plea.

source.text: נַחֲלָתֵ֨נוּ֙ נֶֽהֶפְכָ֣ה לְזָרִ֔ים בָּתֵּ֖ינוּ לְנָכְרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.

en.L: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, \q our houses to foreigners.
en.B: Our inheritance has been handed over to strangers, \q our homes to foreigners.
en.R: The land God gave us as our own has gone to strangers. \q Foreigners live in our homes.

fr.L: Notre héritage a été remis à des inconnus, \q nos maisons à des étrangers.
fr.B: Notre héritage a été livré à des inconnus, \q nos maisons à des étrangers.
fr.R: La terre que Dieu nous avait donnée est passée à des inconnus. \q Des étrangers habitent dans nos maisons.

es.L: Nuestra heredad ha pasado a extraños, \q nuestras casas a extranjeros.
es.B: Nuestra herencia ha sido entregada a extraños, \q nuestros hogares a extranjeros.
es.R: La tierra que Dios nos dio como nuestra ha pasado a manos de extraños. \q Los extranjeros viven en nuestras casas.

sw.L: Urithi wetu umepewa wageni, \q nyumba zetu [zimepewa] watu wa mataifa mengine.
sw.B: Urithi wetu umekabidhiwa wageni, \q nyumba zetu kwa watu wa kigeni.
sw.R: Nchi ambayo Mungu alitupa iwe yetu imechukuliwa na wageni. \q Watu wa kigeni wanaishi katika nyumba zetu.

vi.L: Cơ nghiệp của chúng con đã bị chuyển sang tay người lạ, \q nhà cửa chúng con sang tay người ngoại quốc.
vi.B: Sản nghiệp của chúng con đã bị trao cho người lạ, \q nhà cửa chúng con vào tay người nước ngoài.
vi.R: Đất đai Đức Chúa Trời ban cho chúng con làm của riêng đã về tay người lạ. \q Người nước ngoài sống trong nhà của chúng con.

decisions.choice: inheritance: the land God allotted to Israel's families
decisions.reason: The word (nachalah) is the family land each tribe and clan received when Israel entered Canaan (Numbers 26:52-56; Joshua 13:7). It was held as God's gift and was not meant to pass out of the family (Leviticus 25:23; 1 Kings 21:3). Losing it to outsiders meant losing their place in the land itself.

decisions.choice: strangers ... foreigners: outsiders and people of other nations
decisions.reason: The two words are a pair (Isaiah 1:7; Obadiah 11). They name the conquerors and the people who moved in after them.

decisions.choice: The land God gave us as our own has gone
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" (m1) and gives the second line a subject and verb of its own.

source.text: יְתוֹמִ֤ים הָיִ֨ינוּ֙ וְאֵ֣ין אָ֔ב אִמֹּתֵ֖ינוּ כְּאַלְמָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Orphans we have become, and there is no father; our mothers [are] like widows.

en.L: We have become orphans, without a father; \q our mothers [are] like widows.
en.B: We have become orphans, with no father; \q our mothers are like widows.
en.R: We have become orphans who have no father. \q Our mothers are like widows.

fr.L: Nous sommes devenus des orphelins, sans père ; \q nos mères [sont] comme des veuves.
fr.B: Nous voilà orphelins, privés de père ; \q nos mères sont comme des veuves.
fr.R: Nous sommes devenus des orphelins qui n’ont plus de père. \q Nos mères sont comme des veuves.

es.L: Huérfanos hemos llegado a ser, sin padre; \q nuestras madres [son] como viudas.
es.B: Nos hemos quedado huérfanos, sin padre; \q nuestras madres son como viudas.
es.R: Somos como huérfanos que no tienen padre. \q Nuestras madres son como viudas.

sw.L: Tumekuwa yatima, bila baba; \q mama zetu [ni] kama wajane.
sw.B: Tumekuwa yatima, hatuna baba; \q mama zetu ni kama wajane.
sw.R: Tumekuwa yatima wasio na baba. \q Mama zetu ni kama wajane.

vi.L: Chúng con đã trở thành mồ côi, không cha; \q mẹ chúng con [như] những góa phụ.
vi.B: Chúng con đã thành mồ côi, không còn cha; \q mẹ chúng con như những người góa bụa.
vi.R: Chúng con đã thành những đứa trẻ mồ côi không cha. \q Mẹ chúng con như những người góa bụa.

decisions.choice: orphans and widows: people left without a protector
decisions.reason: In Israel the fatherless and the widow were the people most easily wronged, and God's law singled them out for care (Exodus 22:21-23; Deuteronomy 10:18; 24:17). Many men had been killed or carried off, but the picture is wider: the whole people is left like a family with no one to defend it. "Like widows" may mean their husbands were gone, or that they lived as if they were.

decisions.choice: and there is no father
decisions.reason: The word "and" is in the reading given in the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts but not in the written text. The sense is the same either way.

source.text: מֵימֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּכֶ֣סֶף שָׁתִ֔ינוּ עֵצֵ֖ינוּ בִּמְחִ֥יר יָבֹֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our water for silver we have drunk; our wood for a price comes.

en.L: Our water we have drunk for silver; \q our wood comes at a price.
en.B: We have to pay money for the water we drink; \q our own wood comes to us only at a price.
en.R: We have to pay for our own drinking water. \q We even have to buy our own firewood.

fr.L: Notre eau, nous l’avons bue pour de l’argent ; \q notre bois nous vient contre paiement.
fr.B: Nous devons payer l’eau que nous buvons ; \q notre propre bois ne nous parvient que contre paiement.
fr.R: Nous devons payer notre propre eau à boire. \q Nous devons même acheter notre propre bois pour le feu.

es.L: Nuestra agua la bebemos por plata; \q nuestra leña nos llega por precio.
es.B: Tenemos que pagar dinero por el agua que bebemos; \q nuestra propia leña solo nos llega pagando.
es.R: Tenemos que pagar por nuestra propia agua para beber. \q Hasta tenemos que comprar nuestra propia leña.

sw.L: Maji yetu tumekunywa kwa fedha; \q kuni zetu zinakuja kwa bei.
sw.B: Tunalazimika kulipa fedha kwa maji tunayokunywa; \q kuni zetu wenyewe tunazipata kwa kununua tu.
sw.R: Tunalazimika kulipia maji yetu wenyewe ya kunywa. \q Hata kuni zetu wenyewe tunalazimika kuzinunua.

vi.L: Nước của chúng con, chúng con đã uống bằng bạc; \q củi của chúng con đến bằng giá tiền.
vi.B: Chúng con phải trả tiền để uống nước; \q củi của chính mình cũng phải mua mới có.
vi.R: Chúng con phải trả tiền cho chính nước uống của mình. \q Chúng con thậm chí phải mua củi của chính mình.

decisions.choice: our water ... our wood: basic needs that had been our own
decisions.reason: Water from their own wells and firewood from their own land had cost nothing (compare Deuteronomy 6:11). Now the land belongs to others, and the people must buy back what was once theirs. "Our" is stressed in both lines.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: Silver weighed out was the money of the time (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9).

decisions.choice: for silver
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the metal, which was also the word for money; Balanced and Readable say what it was used as (m2).

source.text: עַ֤ל צַוָּארֵ֨נוּ֙ נִרְדָּ֔פְנוּ יָגַ֖עְנוּ וְלֹ֥א הֽוּנַ֖חלָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Upon our neck we have been pursued; we have grown weary, and not has been given rest to us.

en.L: Upon our necks we are pursued; \q we are weary, and no rest is given to us.
en.B: Our pursuers are at our necks; \q we are worn out, and we are given no rest.
en.R: Our enemies chase us and are close behind us. \q We are tired out, and we get no rest.

fr.L: Sur nos cous nous sommes poursuivis ; \q nous sommes épuisés, et on ne nous donne pas de repos.
fr.B: Nos poursuivants sont à nos trousses ; \q nous sommes épuisés, et on ne nous laisse aucun repos.
fr.R: Nos ennemis nous poursuivent et sont juste derrière nous. \q Nous sommes à bout de forces, et nous n’avons aucun repos.

es.L: Sobre nuestro cuello somos perseguidos; \q estamos cansados, y no se nos da descanso.
es.B: Nuestros perseguidores nos pisan los talones; \q estamos agotados, y no nos dan descanso.
es.R: Nuestros enemigos nos persiguen y casi nos alcanzan. \q Estamos rendidos, y no tenemos descanso.

sw.L: Juu ya shingo zetu tunafuatiwa; \q tumechoka, wala hatupewi pumziko.
sw.B: Wanaotufuatia wako shingoni mwetu; \q tumechoka kabisa, wala hatupewi pumziko.
sw.R: Adui zetu wanatufukuza na wako karibu kabisa nyuma yetu. \q Tumechoka, wala hatupati pumziko.

vi.L: Trên cổ chúng con, chúng con bị đuổi theo; \q chúng con mệt mỏi, và không được cho nghỉ ngơi.
vi.B: Kẻ săn đuổi đã kề sát cổ chúng con; \q chúng con kiệt sức, mà chẳng được nghỉ ngơi.
vi.R: Kẻ thù đuổi theo sát sau lưng chúng con. \q Chúng con mệt lả, và không được nghỉ ngơi.

decisions.choice: upon our necks: pursuers close enough to seize us
alternatives: with a yoke on our necks we are driven
decisions.reason: "On our neck" pictures enemies right behind the people, close enough to grab them. Some suggest that the word "yoke" has dropped out of the text, giving: "with a yoke on our necks we are driven", picturing forced labor as in 1:14. That needs a word not in the Hebrew text, so the text as it stands is kept here.

decisions.choice: and no rest
decisions.reason: The word "and" is in the reading given in the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts but not in the written text. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Our pursuers / Our enemies
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "we are pursued". Balanced and Readable name the ones chasing them.

decisions.choice: "sont à nos trousses"
decisions.reason: French "sur nos cous" does not say "close enough to seize us" (m1); the French idiom for a close chase does, while Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

decisions.choice: "nos pisan los talones"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pictures pursuers at the neck; Spanish says the same thing with its own idiom for a pursuer close behind. Literal keeps the Hebrew picture.

source.text: מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ נָתַ֣נּוּ יָ֔ד אַשּׁ֖וּר לִשְׂבֹּ֥עַֽ לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: [To] Egypt we have given [the] hand, [to] Assyria, to be satisfied [with] bread.

en.L: To Egypt we have given the hand, \q [and to] Assyria, to be satisfied with bread.
en.B: We pledged ourselves to Egypt \q and to Assyria, to get enough bread.
en.R: We made deals with Egypt \q and with Assyria just to get enough food to eat.

fr.L: À l’Égypte nous avons donné la main, \q [et à] l’Assyrie, pour être rassasiés de pain.
fr.B: Nous nous sommes engagés envers l’Égypte \q et envers l’Assyrie, pour avoir assez de pain.
fr.R: Nous avons passé des accords avec l’Égypte \q et avec l’Assyrie, seulement pour avoir assez à manger.

es.L: A Egipto hemos dado la mano, \q [y a] Asiria, para saciarnos de pan.
es.B: Nos sometimos a Egipto \q y a Asiria para conseguir suficiente pan.
es.R: Hicimos tratos con Egipto \q y con Asiria solo para tener suficiente comida.

sw.L: Kwa Misri tumetoa mkono, \q [na kwa] Ashuru, ili kushiba mkate.
sw.B: Tulijitia chini ya Misri \q na chini ya Ashuru, ili tupate mkate wa kutosha.
sw.R: Tulifanya mapatano na Misri \q na Ashuru ili tu tupate chakula cha kutosha.

vi.L: Với Ai Cập chúng con đã đưa tay, \q [và với] A-si-ri, để được no bánh.
vi.B: Chúng con đã cam kết với Ai Cập \q và với A-si-ri, để có đủ bánh ăn.
vi.R: Chúng con đã thỏa thuận với Ai Cập \q và A-si-ri chỉ để có đủ thức ăn.

decisions.choice: given the hand: pledged loyalty, submitted
alternatives: held out our hand to beg
decisions.reason: To give the hand is to make a pledge or yield to someone's rule (2 Kings 10:15; 1 Chronicles 29:24; Ezra 10:19). Some take it as holding out the hand to beg, but the phrase elsewhere means a binding agreement.

decisions.choice: Egypt and Assyria: the great powers Israel leaned on
decisions.reason: Egypt to the south and Assyria to the north were the empires Israel and Judah turned to for help instead of trusting God (Jeremiah 2:18, 36; Hosea 7:11; 12:2). The verse may look back on that history, leading into the fathers' sin of verse 7, or it may use the old names for the powers of the day, when Babylon ruled the north.

decisions.choice: bread: food
decisions.reason: Bread stands for food in general, as often (Genesis 3:19).

decisions.choice: pledged ourselves to / made deals with
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the gesture meant (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: אֲבֹתֵ֤ינוּ חָֽטְאוּ֙ וְאֵינָ֔ם וַאֲנַ֖חְנוּ עֲוֺנֹתֵיהֶ֥ם סָבָֽלְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our fathers sinned, and they are not; and we their iniquities have borne.

en.L: Our fathers sinned, and they are no more; \q and we have borne their iniquities.
en.B: Our fathers sinned, and they are gone, \q and we carry the weight of their guilt.
en.R: Our ancestors sinned, and they are dead now. \q But we are the ones suffering for their sins.

fr.L: Nos pères ont péché, et ils ne sont plus ; \q et nous, nous avons porté leurs fautes.
fr.B: Nos pères ont péché, et ils ne sont plus, \q et nous portons le poids de leur faute.
fr.R: Nos ancêtres ont péché, et maintenant ils sont morts. \q Mais c’est nous qui souffrons à cause de leurs péchés.

es.L: Nuestros padres pecaron, y ya no existen; \q y nosotros hemos cargado con sus iniquidades.
es.B: Nuestros padres pecaron, y ya no están, \q y nosotros llevamos el peso de su culpa.
es.R: Nuestros antepasados pecaron, y ahora están muertos. \q Pero somos nosotros los que sufrimos por sus pecados.

sw.L: Baba zetu walitenda dhambi, nao hawapo; \q nasi tumeyabeba maovu yao.
sw.B: Baba zetu walitenda dhambi, nao wamekwisha kufa, \q nasi tunaubeba mzigo wa hatia yao.
sw.R: Mababu zetu walitenda dhambi, nao sasa wamekufa. \q Lakini sisi ndio tunaoteseka kwa ajili ya dhambi zao.

vi.L: Tổ phụ chúng con đã phạm tội, và họ không còn nữa; \q còn chúng con đã mang lấy sự gian ác của họ.
vi.B: Tổ phụ chúng con đã phạm tội, và nay họ không còn nữa, \q còn chúng con phải gánh lấy tội lỗi của họ.
vi.R: Tổ tiên chúng con đã phạm tội, và nay họ đã chết. \q Nhưng chính chúng con phải chịu khổ vì tội lỗi của họ.

decisions.choice: the fathers sinned, and we bear it
decisions.reason: The complaint echoes the saying quoted in Jeremiah 31:29 and Ezekiel 18:2, "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge." Both prophets answer that each person will die for his own sin (Jeremiah 31:30; Ezekiel 18:20). Here it is a cry of grief rather than a denial of guilt: the same people confess "we have sinned" in verse 16. Compare Exodus 20:5.

decisions.choice: bear their iniquities: suffer the punishment their sins brought
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity ('awon) covers the wrong, the guilt and its penalty. To "bear" it is to carry the consequences (Numbers 14:33-34; Ezekiel 4:4-6).

decisions.choice: and they are not; and we
decisions.reason: The two "and"s are in the reading given in the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts but not in the written text. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: ancestors ... suffering for their sins
decisions.reason: Readable says "ancestors" for the earlier generations meant by "fathers", and "suffering for their sins" for bearing their iniquities (m2).

source.text: עֲבָדִים֙ מָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֔נוּ פֹּרֵ֖ק אֵ֥ין מִיָּדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Slaves have ruled over us; [one] tearing away there is not from their hand.

en.L: Slaves rule over us; \q there is no one to tear [us] from their hand.
en.B: Slaves rule over us, \q and no one rescues us from their power.
en.R: Slaves have become our rulers, \q and there is no one to save us from them.

fr.L: Des esclaves dominent sur nous ; \q il n’y a personne pour [nous] arracher de leur main.
fr.B: Des esclaves nous gouvernent, \q et personne ne nous délivre de leur pouvoir.
fr.R: Des esclaves sont devenus nos maîtres, \q et personne ne peut nous sauver d’eux.

es.L: Esclavos se han enseñoreado de nosotros; \q no hay quien [nos] arranque de su mano.
es.B: Esclavos nos gobiernan, \q y nadie nos libra de su poder.
es.R: Unos esclavos se han convertido en nuestros gobernantes, \q y no hay nadie que nos salve de ellos.

sw.L: Watumwa wanatutawala; \q hakuna anayetupokonya mkononi mwao.
sw.B: Watumwa wanatutawala, \q wala hakuna anayetuokoa kutoka katika mamlaka yao.
sw.R: Watumwa wamekuwa watawala wetu, \q wala hakuna wa kutuokoa kutoka kwao.

vi.L: Những kẻ nô lệ cai trị chúng con; \q không ai giật [chúng con] khỏi tay chúng.
vi.B: Những kẻ nô lệ cai trị chúng con, \q và không ai giải cứu chúng con khỏi quyền lực của chúng.
vi.R: Những kẻ nô lệ đã trở thành người cai trị chúng con, \q và không ai cứu chúng con khỏi tay chúng.

decisions.choice: slaves: people of low rank, now in power
decisions.reason: The world is turned upside down: those who were servants rule (Proverbs 30:21-22). They may be the officials of the Babylonian king, who were called his servants (2 Kings 25:8), now lording it over Judah's people.

decisions.choice: tear away: rescue by force
decisions.reason: The verb (paraq) means to tear something off or away, and so to snatch someone out of an enemy's grip (Psalm 136:24).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "slaves" because the shame of low-ranking people ruling over them is the point (m1); "servants" would lose it.

decisions.choice: from their power / from them
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ nô lệ" at every level
decisions.reason: The point is that men of the lowest rank now rule; "đầy tớ" is kept for God's servants and for "your servant" in prayer, and "nô lệ" for slavery itself, which is meant here.

source.text: בְּנַפְשֵׁ֨נוּ֙ נָבִ֣יא לַחְמֵ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: With our life we bring our bread, because of [the] sword of the wilderness.

en.L: At [the risk of] our lives we bring [in] our bread, \q because of the sword of the wilderness.
en.B: We risk our lives to bring in our bread, \q because of the sword in the wilderness.
en.R: We risk our lives just to get food, \q because armed raiders attack us in the open country.

fr.L: Au [péril de] notre vie nous rapportons notre pain, \q à cause de l’épée du désert.
fr.B: Nous risquons notre vie pour rapporter notre pain, \q à cause de l’épée qui rôde dans le désert.
fr.R: Nous risquons notre vie juste pour trouver de la nourriture, \q parce que des pillards armés nous attaquent dans la campagne.

es.L: Con [riesgo de] nuestra vida traemos nuestro pan, \q a causa de la espada del desierto.
es.B: Arriesgamos la vida para traer nuestro pan, \q por causa de la espada en el desierto.
es.R: Arriesgamos la vida solo para conseguir comida, \q porque bandidos armados nos atacan en el campo abierto.

sw.L: Kwa [kuhatarisha] uhai wetu tunaleta mkate wetu, \q kwa sababu ya upanga wa nyikani.
sw.B: Tunahatarisha maisha yetu ili kuleta mkate wetu, \q kwa sababu ya upanga ulioko nyikani.
sw.R: Tunahatarisha maisha yetu ili tu kupata chakula, \q kwa sababu wavamizi wenye silaha wanatushambulia porini.

vi.L: Với [nguy hiểm đến] mạng sống, chúng con mang bánh của chúng con [về], \q vì gươm của hoang mạc.
vi.B: Chúng con liều mạng sống để mang bánh về, \q vì gươm giáo trong hoang mạc.
vi.R: Chúng con liều mạng chỉ để kiếm thức ăn, \q vì bọn cướp có vũ khí tấn công chúng con nơi đồng trống.

decisions.choice: with our life: at the risk of our lives
decisions.reason: The same expression is used of David's men fetching water at the risk of their lives (2 Samuel 23:17).

decisions.choice: the sword of the wilderness: raiders from the open country
decisions.reason: Those who went out to harvest or to fetch grain could be attacked by armed bands roaming the dry country beyond the towns (compare Jeremiah 12:12; 41:8).

decisions.choice: armed raiders attack us in the open country
decisions.reason: Readable explains the "sword of the wilderness" (m2).

source.text: עוֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Our skin like an oven has grown hot because of [the] burning heat of famine.

en.L: Our skin has grown hot like an oven \q because of the scorching heat of famine.
en.B: Our skin burns like an oven \q with the fever of hunger.
en.R: Our skin is as hot as an oven, \q because hunger has made us burn with fever.

fr.L: Notre peau est devenue brûlante comme un four \q à cause des ardeurs de la famine.
fr.B: Notre peau brûle comme un four \q sous la fièvre de la faim.
fr.R: Notre peau est aussi chaude qu’un four, \q parce que la faim nous donne de la fièvre.

es.L: Nuestra piel se ha calentado como un horno \q a causa del ardor abrasador del hambre.
es.B: Nuestra piel arde como un horno \q por la fiebre del hambre.
es.R: Tenemos la piel tan caliente como un horno, \q porque el hambre nos hace arder de fiebre.

sw.L: Ngozi yetu imepata moto kama tanuru \q kwa sababu ya joto kali la njaa.
sw.B: Ngozi yetu inawaka kama tanuru \q kwa homa ya njaa.
sw.R: Ngozi yetu ina joto kama tanuru, \q kwa sababu njaa imetufanya tuwe na homa kali.

vi.L: Da chúng con đã nóng như lò \q vì cơn nóng bỏng của nạn đói.
vi.B: Da chúng con nóng rực như lò \q vì cơn sốt của nạn đói.
vi.R: Da chúng con nóng như lò lửa, \q vì cơn đói khiến chúng con lên cơn sốt.

decisions.choice: grown hot: burning with fever
decisions.reason: The verb is used of being warm or stirred (Genesis 43:30; Hosea 11:8). Here starvation brings on fever. Some take it as "blackened", like the skin of the starving in 4:8.

decisions.choice: scorching heat: the raging burning of hunger
decisions.reason: The word (zal'afah) is used of scorching wind (Psalm 11:6) and of burning anger (Psalm 119:53). It pictures famine as a fire inside the body.

decisions.choice: fever
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the burning as fever (m1, m2).

source.text: נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Women in Zion they have raped, virgins in [the] cities of Judah.

en.L: Women in Zion they have raped, \q virgins in the cities of Judah.
en.B: Women were raped in Zion, \q virgins in the towns of Judah.
en.R: Enemy soldiers raped the women in Zion \q and the young unmarried women in the towns of Judah.

fr.L: Ils ont violé des femmes dans Sion, \q des vierges dans les villes de Juda.
fr.B: Des femmes ont été violées dans Sion, \q des vierges dans les villes de Juda.
fr.R: Des soldats ennemis ont violé les femmes de Sion \q et les jeunes filles des villes de Juda.

es.L: A las mujeres en Sion violaron, \q a las vírgenes en las ciudades de Judá.
es.B: En Sion violaron a las mujeres, \q y a las vírgenes en los pueblos de Judá.
es.R: Los soldados enemigos violaron a las mujeres en Sion \q y a las muchachas solteras en los pueblos de Judá.

sw.L: Wanawake katika Sayuni wamewabaka, \q mabikira katika miji ya Yuda.
sw.B: Wanawake walibakwa katika Sayuni, \q mabikira katika miji ya Yuda.
sw.R: Askari wa adui waliwabaka wanawake katika Sayuni \q na wasichana ambao hawajaolewa katika miji ya Yuda.

vi.L: Phụ nữ ở Si-ôn, chúng đã hãm hiếp, \q các trinh nữ trong các thành của Giu-đa.
vi.B: Phụ nữ ở Si-ôn bị hãm hiếp, \q các trinh nữ trong các thành của Giu-đa cũng vậy.
vi.R: Quân lính kẻ thù đã hãm hiếp phụ nữ ở Si-ôn \q và các thiếu nữ chưa chồng trong các thành của Giu-đa.

decisions.choice: raped: forced and humiliated
decisions.reason: The verb ('anah) means to humble or afflict; used of a woman it means rape (Genesis 34:2; 2 Samuel 13:12, 14). The conquerors did this to the women of the land, as the covenant curses had warned (Deuteronomy 28:30).

decisions.choice: virgins: young women not yet married
decisions.reason: The word (betulah) names a young woman of marriageable age who has not married (Deuteronomy 22:19).

decisions.choice: Zion ... the cities of Judah: the whole land
decisions.reason: The pair covers Jerusalem and every town around it: no place was spared.

decisions.choice: were raped
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a passive and leaves the doers unnamed, as the Hebrew does not name them either.

decisions.choice: Enemy soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" were, the conquering army.

decisions.choice: "des vierges" at Balanced here
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in the book Balanced says "jeunes filles"; here the outrage done to unmarried women is the point (m2), and the English Balanced keeps "virgins", so French does too.

source.text: שָׂרִים֙ בְּיָדָ֣ם נִתְל֔וּ פְּנֵ֥י זְקֵנִ֖ים לֹ֥א נֶהְדָּֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Princes by their hand have been hung up; [the] faces of elders have not been honored.

en.L: Princes have been hung up by their hands; \q the faces of elders have not been honored.
en.B: Officials were hung up by their hands; \q no respect was shown to the elders.
en.R: Our leaders were hung up by their hands. \q No one showed respect to the elders.

fr.L: Des chefs ont été pendus par leurs mains ; \q la face des anciens n’a pas été honorée.
fr.B: Des chefs ont été pendus par les mains ; \q on n’a montré aucun respect aux anciens.
fr.R: Nos dirigeants ont été pendus par les mains. \q Personne n’a respecté les anciens.

es.L: Los príncipes fueron colgados de sus manos; \q los rostros de los ancianos no fueron honrados.
es.B: Los jefes fueron colgados de las manos; \q a los ancianos no se les mostró respeto.
es.R: Nuestros dirigentes fueron colgados de las manos. \q Nadie respetó a los ancianos.

sw.L: Wakuu wametundikwa kwa mikono yao; \q nyuso za wazee hazikuheshimiwa.
sw.B: Maafisa walitundikwa kwa mikono yao; \q wazee hawakuonyeshwa heshima.
sw.R: Viongozi wetu walitundikwa kwa mikono yao. \q Hakuna aliyewaheshimu wazee.

vi.L: Các thủ lĩnh bị treo lên bởi tay họ; \q mặt các trưởng lão đã không được tôn trọng.
vi.B: Các quan chức bị treo lên bằng tay; \q các trưởng lão chẳng được ai kính trọng.
vi.R: Các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng con bị treo lên bằng hai tay. \q Chẳng ai kính trọng các trưởng lão.

decisions.choice: hung up by their hands
alternatives: princes were hanged by their hand [the enemies']
decisions.reason: "By their hand" may mean the princes were strung up by their own hands, a cruel torture or a way of displaying their bodies. It may also mean they were hanged by the enemies' hand, "their" pointing back to the slaves of verse 8. Hanging up a body for all to see was a mark of disgrace (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Joshua 10:26; 2 Samuel 4:12).

decisions.choice: the faces of elders were not honored
decisions.reason: The law says "honor the face of the old man" (Leviticus 19:32), with the same words. The conquerors showed no respect for age or rank.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: As the book-wide table has it for sar: Literal "princes", Balanced "officials", Readable "leaders".

decisions.choice: no respect was shown
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "the faces ... were not honored" means.

source.text: בַּחוּרִים֙ טְח֣וֹן נָשָׂ֔אוּ וּנְעָרִ֖ים בָּעֵ֥ץ כָּשָֽׁלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Young men [the] mill have carried, and youths under [the] wood have stumbled.

en.L: Young men have carried the mill, \q and boys have stumbled under the wood.
en.B: Young men haul the grinding stones, \q and boys stagger under loads of wood.
en.R: Young men are forced to grind grain like slaves, \q and boys stumble under heavy loads of firewood.

fr.L: Les jeunes hommes ont porté la meule, \q et les garçons ont trébuché sous le bois.
fr.B: Les jeunes hommes traînent les meules, \q et les garçons chancellent sous des charges de bois.
fr.R: Les jeunes hommes sont obligés de moudre le grain comme des esclaves, \q et les garçons trébuchent sous de lourdes charges de bois pour le feu.

es.L: Los jóvenes han cargado la piedra de moler, \q y los muchachos han tropezado bajo la leña.
es.B: Los jóvenes arrastran las piedras de moler, \q y los muchachos se tambalean bajo cargas de leña.
es.R: Obligan a los jóvenes a moler grano como esclavos, \q y los muchachos tropiezan bajo pesadas cargas de leña.

sw.L: Vijana wamebeba jiwe la kusagia, \q na wavulana wamejikwaa chini ya kuni.
sw.B: Vijana wanakokota mawe ya kusagia, \q na wavulana wanapepesuka chini ya mizigo ya kuni.
sw.R: Vijana wanalazimishwa kusaga nafaka kama watumwa, \q na wavulana wanajikwaa chini ya mizigo mizito ya kuni.

vi.L: Các trai trẻ đã mang cối xay, \q và các thiếu niên đã vấp ngã dưới [gánh] củi.
vi.B: Trai trẻ phải khuân đá cối xay, \q và thiếu niên lảo đảo dưới những bó củi.
vi.R: Trai trẻ bị bắt phải xay bột như nô lệ, \q và các cậu bé vấp ngã dưới những gánh củi nặng.

decisions.choice: the mill: the heavy grinding stones
decisions.reason: This word (techon) is found only here; it comes from the verb for grinding. The young men either carry the millstones or do the grinding themselves.

decisions.choice: grinding: the work of slaves and prisoners
decisions.reason: Grinding grain by hand was the lowest work, done by slave girls and prisoners (Exodus 11:5; Judges 16:21; Isaiah 47:2). Young men in their strength are put to it as captives.

decisions.choice: under the wood: carrying firewood
decisions.reason: Cutting and carrying wood was labor put on a subject people (Joshua 9:21-27). The boys are too young for the loads.

decisions.choice: are forced to grind grain like slaves
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1, m2); "forced" and "like slaves" say what Balanced leaves implied.

source.text: זְקֵנִים֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר שָׁבָ֔תוּ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מִנְּגִינָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Elders from [the] gate have ceased, young men from their music.

en.L: Elders have ceased from the gate, \q young men from their music.
en.B: The elders are gone from the city gate, \q the young men from their music.
en.R: The elders no longer sit at the city gate. \q The young men no longer play their music.

fr.L: Les anciens ont cessé [de venir] à la porte, \q les jeunes hommes, leur musique.
fr.B: Les anciens ont disparu de la porte de la ville, \q les jeunes hommes ont cessé leur musique.
fr.R: Les anciens ne s’assoient plus à la porte de la ville. \q Les jeunes hommes ne jouent plus leur musique.

es.L: Los ancianos han dejado la puerta, \q los jóvenes su música.
es.B: Los ancianos ya no están en la puerta de la ciudad, \q ni los jóvenes con su música.
es.R: Los ancianos ya no se sientan a la puerta de la ciudad. \q Los jóvenes ya no tocan su música.

sw.L: Wazee wameacha [kuketi] langoni, \q vijana [wameacha] muziki wao.
sw.B: Wazee wametoweka langoni mwa mji, \q vijana wameacha muziki wao.
sw.R: Wazee hawaketi tena langoni mwa mji. \q Vijana hawapigi tena muziki wao.

vi.L: Các trưởng lão đã thôi khỏi cổng thành, \q các trai trẻ [thôi] khỏi âm nhạc của mình.
vi.B: Các trưởng lão không còn ở nơi cổng thành, \q các trai trẻ đã bỏ cuộc vui đàn hát.
vi.R: Các trưởng lão không còn ngồi nơi cổng thành. \q Các trai trẻ không còn chơi nhạc nữa.

decisions.choice: the gate: where the elders sat
decisions.reason: The open space at a town's gate was where the elders met to judge cases and settle the town's business (Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:1-2; Job 29:7). The town's life has stopped.

decisions.choice: music: songs played on instruments
decisions.reason: The word (neginah) is music played on stringed instruments and the songs that went with it (Isaiah 38:20; compare 3:14, where the people make Zion their mocking song).

decisions.choice: the city gate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which gate is meant.

source.text: שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ לִבֵּ֔נוּ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְאֵ֖בֶל מְחֹלֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Has ceased [the] joy of our heart; has been turned to mourning our dancing.

en.L: The joy of our heart has ceased; \q our dancing has been turned to mourning.
en.B: Joy has gone from our hearts; \q our dancing has turned into mourning.
en.R: There is no more joy in our hearts. \q Instead of dancing, we mourn.

fr.L: La joie de notre cœur a cessé ; \q notre danse s’est changée en deuil.
fr.B: La joie a quitté nos cœurs ; \q nos danses se sont changées en deuil.
fr.R: Il n’y a plus de joie dans nos cœurs. \q Au lieu de danser, nous sommes en deuil.

es.L: Ha cesado el gozo de nuestro corazón; \q nuestra danza se ha convertido en luto.
es.B: La alegría se ha ido de nuestro corazón; \q nuestras danzas se han convertido en luto.
es.R: Ya no hay alegría en nuestro corazón. \q En lugar de bailar, estamos de luto.

sw.L: Furaha ya moyo wetu imekoma; \q kucheza kwetu kumegeuzwa kuwa maombolezo.
sw.B: Furaha imetoweka mioyoni mwetu; \q kucheza kwetu kumegeuka kuwa maombolezo.
sw.R: Hakuna tena furaha mioyoni mwetu. \q Badala ya kucheza, tunaomboleza.

vi.L: Niềm vui của lòng chúng con đã dứt; \q sự nhảy múa của chúng con đã đổi thành tang chế.
vi.B: Niềm vui đã lìa khỏi lòng chúng con; \q điệu múa của chúng con đã hóa thành tang tóc.
vi.R: Lòng chúng con chẳng còn chút niềm vui. \q Thay vì nhảy múa, chúng con than khóc.

decisions.choice: dancing turned to mourning
decisions.reason: The line reverses the praise of Psalm 30:12, "you have turned my mourning into dancing", and the promise of Jeremiah 31:13. The joy that once filled Jerusalem has ended, as Jeremiah warned (Jeremiah 7:34; 16:9).

decisions.choice: has ceased
decisions.reason: The verb "cease" repeats from verse 14: elders, music and joy have all stopped.

decisions.choice: Instead of dancing, we mourn
decisions.reason: Readable makes the second line a short active sentence.

source.text: נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ אֽוֹי־נָ֥א לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Has fallen [the] crown of our head; woe now to us, for we have sinned!

en.L: The crown of our head has fallen; \q woe now to us, for we have sinned!
en.B: Our crown has fallen from our head; \q woe to us, because we have sinned!
en.R: We have lost our honor, like a crown fallen from our heads. \q How terrible this is for us, because we have sinned!

fr.L: La couronne de notre tête est tombée ; \q malheur donc à nous, car nous avons péché !
fr.B: La couronne est tombée de notre tête ; \q malheur à nous, car nous avons péché !
fr.R: Nous avons perdu notre honneur, comme une couronne tombée de notre tête. \q Quel malheur pour nous, parce que nous avons péché !

es.L: Ha caído la corona de nuestra cabeza; \q ¡ay ahora de nosotros, porque hemos pecado!
es.B: Se ha caído la corona de nuestra cabeza; \q ¡ay de nosotros, porque hemos pecado!
es.R: Hemos perdido nuestra honra, como una corona que se cae de la cabeza. \q ¡Qué terrible es esto para nosotros, porque hemos pecado!

sw.L: Taji ya kichwa chetu imeanguka; \q ole wetu sasa, kwa maana tumetenda dhambi!
sw.B: Taji yetu imeanguka kutoka kichwani mwetu; \q ole wetu, kwa sababu tumetenda dhambi!
sw.R: Tumepoteza heshima yetu, kama taji iliyoanguka kutoka vichwani mwetu. \q Mambo ni mabaya sana kwetu, kwa sababu tumetenda dhambi!

vi.L: Mão miện của đầu chúng con đã rơi; \q khốn cho chúng con bây giờ, vì chúng con đã phạm tội!
vi.B: Mão miện đã rơi khỏi đầu chúng con; \q khốn cho chúng con, vì chúng con đã phạm tội!
vi.R: Chúng con đã mất hết danh dự, như mão miện rơi khỏi đầu. \q Thật khốn khổ cho chúng con, vì chúng con đã phạm tội!

decisions.choice: the crown of our head: our honor and glory
decisions.reason: The crown stands for the honor of the people and its city, perhaps also for its king (Jeremiah 13:18; Job 19:9).

decisions.choice: for we have sinned: the people confess their own guilt
decisions.reason: After blaming the fathers in verse 7, the people own that they too have sinned (compare 1:18; 3:42). The prayer holds both together.

decisions.choice: woe now
decisions.reason: The cry of grief "woe" is sharpened by a small word of urging, "now" or "please".

decisions.choice: We have lost our honor, like a crown ... How terrible this is for us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the crown (m1) and says "how terrible this is for us" for the cry "woe to us", as Isaiah's Readable does.

decisions.choice: "¡ay de nosotros!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible es esto para nosotros!" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry of woe said of oneself is worded as in the Spanish Isaiah ("¡Ay de mí!" / "¡Qué terrible es esto para mí!"), here in the plural.

decisions.choice: "ole wetu" (L, B), "Mambo ni mabaya sana kwetu" (R) for 'oy lanu
decisions.reason: The cry of woe spoken of oneself follows the wording settled for Isaiah and Jeremiah ("Ole wangu" at Literal and Balanced, a plain statement at Readable), here in the plural.

source.text: עַל־זֶ֗ה הָיָ֤ה דָוֶה֙ לִבֵּ֔נוּ עַל־אֵ֖לֶּה חָשְׁכ֥וּ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because of this has become faint our heart, because of these have grown dark our eyes,

en.L: Because of this our heart has become faint, \q because of these things our eyes have grown dim,
en.B: Because of this our hearts are sick, \q because of these things our eyes grow dim,
en.R: That is why we feel sick at heart. \q That is why our eyes are dim with tears.

fr.L: À cause de cela notre cœur est devenu malade, \q à cause de ces [choses] nos yeux se sont obscurcis,
fr.B: C’est pour cela que nos cœurs sont malades, \q pour cela que nos yeux s’obscurcissent,
fr.R: Voilà pourquoi nous avons le cœur malade. \q Voilà pourquoi nos yeux sont voilés de larmes.

es.L: Por esto se ha debilitado nuestro corazón, \q por estas cosas se han oscurecido nuestros ojos,

decisions.choice: because of this ... because of these: pointing back and forward
decisions.reason: "This" points back to the sin and loss of verse 16, and "these things" to all the suffering the prayer has described. Verse 18 adds a third "because of": Mount Zion. The three phrases build to the ruined temple hill as the heart of their grief.

decisions.choice: a faint heart and dim eyes: grief that drains strength
decisions.reason: The same word for a sick or faint heart is used in 1:13 and 1:22. Eyes grow dim from weeping and sorrow (2:11; Job 17:7).

decisions.reason: Readable says what dims the eyes (m2).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end with a comma because verse 18 continues the list of reasons; Readable makes each verse a sentence.

decisions.choice: jackals: wild animals that haunt ruins
decisions.reason: The word (shu'al) can mean fox or jackal. Jackals roam in packs and live among ruins and scavenge the dead (Psalm 63:11), which fits a deserted city best. Foxes are also possible.

decisions.choice: Mount Zion desolate: the temple hill abandoned
decisions.reason: Mount Zion was the hill of the temple, the place God chose to dwell (Psalm 132:13-14). Now it is left to wild animals, as Micah had warned (Micah 3:12; Jeremiah 26:18).

decisions.choice: We grieve for
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and says plainly that the ruin of Zion is a cause of their grief (verse 17, m1).

decisions.choice: "chacales"
decisions.reason: The animals that haunt ruins are named as the English and the meaning decision name them; older Spanish versions have "zorras".

decisions.choice: you, LORD, sit forever: God's reign stands when Zion has fallen
decisions.reason: The "you" is emphatic. Set against the ruined hill of verse 18, the prayer turns to the one throne that has not fallen. The same confession opens Psalm 102:13, and Psalm 9:8 and 29:10 speak of God sitting as king forever.

decisions.choice: sit: sit enthroned, reign
decisions.reason: Used of a king, "sit" means to sit on the throne and rule (1 Kings 1:46; Psalm 29:10).

decisions.choice: bring us back, and we will return: God must act first
decisions.reason: The same verb (shuv) is used twice: "cause us to turn" and "we will turn". It means both coming home and turning back to God in repentance. The people ask God to do what they cannot do alone, in the words of Jeremiah 31:18, "Bring me back, and I will return."

decisions.choice: renew our days as of old: give back the life we had before
decisions.reason: "As of old" (qedem) looks back to the days before the disaster, when the city stood and God was with his people (Micah 7:14; Malachi 3:4).

decisions.choice: we will return
decisions.reason: The reading in the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts has a longer form of the verb ("let us return"); the written text has the shorter form. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end with a comma because verse 22 continues the sentence (verse 22, m1). Readable ends the plea here and links verse 22 with "Do this".

decisions.choice: our lives

decisions.choice: "Haznos volver ... y volveremos"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb twice: God brings the people back, and they return. Literal keeps one Spanish verb for both; "volver" is the word used for turning back to God through these books (3:40).

decisions.choice: One verb repeated for the two halves of "bring us back ... and we will return": "trở lại" (Literal), "quay về ... trở về" (Balanced), "trở về ... quay về" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb twice, God turning the people and the people turning; Vietnamese pairs words from the same family so the echo, and the order (God acts first), stay clear.

decisions.choice: unless you have utterly rejected us
alternatives: but instead you have utterly rejected us
even if you had utterly rejected us
Or have you utterly rejected us?
decisions.reason: The last verse is hard. The two little words (ki 'im) can mean "unless", and that reading is followed here: the plea of verse 21 stands, with the fear that God's rejection might be final. Other readings are possible: "but instead you have utterly rejected us", a bitter last word after the plea; "even if you had utterly rejected us and were very angry", pleading in spite of it; a question, "Or have you utterly rejected us? Are you angry with us beyond measure?"; or "for if you had utterly rejected us, your anger would be beyond measure". The book ends without an answer.

decisions.choice: utterly rejected
decisions.reason: The verb "reject" is doubled for emphasis: rejected completely.

decisions.choice: the fear of final rejection and the hope of 3:31
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 had confessed that "the Lord will not reject forever" (3:31-32). The closing verse keeps that hope and the fear side by side and leaves the outcome with God.

decisions.choice: verse 21 repeated after verse 22
decisions.reason: When Lamentations is read aloud in the synagogue, verse 21 is read again after verse 22, so that the reading ends with the plea for restoration rather than the fear of rejection. The same is done at the end of Isaiah, the Twelve Prophets (Malachi) and Ecclesiastes.

decisions.choice: Do this unless
decisions.reason: Readable ended verse 21 as a sentence, so it repeats the request in two words before "unless" (m1).

decisions.choice: your anger against us knows no limit / has no end
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "you have been angry with us to the utmost" into a phrase about God's anger.
